title: Connectivity accelerator: design notes & terraform patterns (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft of a customer-facing "accelerator" for VPC and on-prem connectivity used by Solutions and Private Deployments teams. The goal is to provide minimal-complexity reference patterns + Terraform module recommendations + a safe cutover plan that can be adapted per customer. This doc focuses on connectivity topologies, IP strategy, egress controls, and a phased upgrade path for tenants currently on shared networking or older Terraform modules.

High-level principles:
- Keep the default topology opinionated and small: one control VPC + per-tenant data subnets.
- Make modules composition-friendly: provide small, testable primitives instead of a single monolith.
- Favor idempotent, reversible operations for cutovers.
- Provide strong validation and smoke-tests that are platform-agnostic.
- Separate security controls from routing: NAT/proxy and firewall rules are managed in a dedicated network module.

Reference topologies (3 patterns):
1) Minimal managed VPC (recommended starter)
   - Single VPC with 3 AZ subnets: control-plane, model-serving, and egress-proxy.
   - Internet egress via a centralized NAT/proxy in the egress-proxy subnet.
   - Peering or private link to customer VPC for control-plane APIs.
   - Use this for small customers or early pilots.

2) Tenant-isolated VPCs (medium)
   - Per-tenant VPCs for data isolation. Shared control-plane VPC peered to each tenant VPC with documented route filters.
   - BGP/MPLS cross connect option for onprem/colo customers.
   - Egress policies can be per-tenant or centralized depending on compliance needs.

3) Air-gapped / On-prem (enterprise)
   - Full private deployment: control plane deployed in customer environment or in VPC with tight express-route to onprem.
   - No public egress unless explicitly allowed; use approved egress appliance.
   - Support for HSM/KMS integration and audit logging.

IP addressing and allocation:
- Recommendation: allocate a /16 for the Redwood-managed block per region, split into /20 chunks per tenant and additional /24 pools for shared services.
- Use deterministic allocation in Terraform state via a central allocator module to avoid overlaps.
- Document rules for bring-your-own-CIDR customers: require at least /24 for each service subnet.

Terraform module design notes (patterns):
- Break modules into primitives: vpc-core, subnet, route-table, nat-gateway, vpn-bgp, interconnect, fw-rules.
- Expose only stable inputs: cidr_block, az_count, tenancy, tags, enable_flow_logs. Change other params through composition.
- Keep lifecycle management explicit: for resources that require replacement on drift, provide a boolean flag to force-recreate during controlled maintenance window.
- State isolation: recommend separate state per customer and per environment (staging/prod). Use remote state locking (S3/consul/ backend).
- Example module mapping:
  - redwood/vpc-core: creates VPC, base route tables, DNS host zone integration hook.
  - redwood/tenant-subnet: creates the three recommended subnets and registers them in a central inventory.
  - redwood/bgp-vpn: small wrapper for cloud VPN or provider-specific crossconnect.

Terraform upgrade path (from legacy modules):
Phase A: inventory + smoke testing\  - Run discovery to capture current CIDRs, peering, and NAT usage.\  - Run smoke tests: control-plane API reachability, health-check endpoints, outbound egress test.
Phase B: prepare new modules in parallel\  - Deploy redwood/vpc-core into a staging workspace with identical inputs.\  - Validate resource names, tags, and flow logs.
Phase C: dual-run and traffic mirroring\  - For serving endpoints, enable traffic mirroring or shadow routing where supported and feasible.\  - Use DNS weight-based canary where possible (10-90 split).
Phase D: cutover and rollback plan\  - Cutover window: pre-scheduled maintenance.\  - Verification checklist: BGP sessions established, control-plane latencies within SLO, no packet loss on key tunnels.\  - Rollback: re-apply legacy state (keep legacy state accessible) and revert DNS weights; automation should support fast revert.

Cutover checklist (practical):
- Pre-checks: backup current Terraform states; export current route tables and peering configs.\- Stakeholders: list primary SRE, Solutions engineer, Customer network owner, Security reviewer.\- Test smoke steps: curl control-plane health, open port checks, egress IP verification.\- During cutover: monitor metrics (BGP flaps, RTT to control-plane, token latency percentiles).\- Post-cutover: run end-to-end workload tests and ramp traffic gradually over 30-60 minutes.

Validation and observability:
- Ensure VPC flow logs are enabled by default in a low-cost mode for 30 days, then roll to archived storage.\- Provide synthetic probes from each AZ to control-plane and to an external egress test endpoint.\- Tagging convention: redwood:tenant, redwood:env, redwood:role. Filters in observability rely on consistent tags.

Security considerations:
- Defense-in-depth: use firewall module to restrict all inter-subnet traffic unless explicitly allowed by ACLs.\- Secrets: prefer customer-managed KMS; encrypt Terraform state at rest and in transit.\- Access: require customer approval for BGP exports; only platform SREs have automation-level keys.

Operational playbook snippets (short):
- Recreate NAT instance safely:\  1) spin new NAT in same AZ with new IPs\  2) attach to egress route table\  3) validate outbound reachability\  4) remove old NAT only after 5 minutes of stable health.

- BGP flap mitigation:\  1) lower BGP timers temporarily\  2) advertise less-specific routes as temporary holdback\  3) escalate to network team if >3 flaps in 15 minutes.

Testing matrix (minimum):
- Control-plane reachability from each tenant subnet.\- Latency and packet loss to model-serving endpoints.
- Egress IP confirmation for audit.
- KMS key usage test for encryption-at-rest.

Common gotchas and lessons learned (ops notes):
- Overlapping CIDRs are the most common deployment showstopper; always run allocator dry-run early.
- Terraform drift against provider-managed resources tends to surface after upgrades; ensure reconciliation scripts are ready.
- DNS TTL and slow propagation can make incremental cutovers look worse than they are; use canary weights not pure DNS swaps for critical endpoints.

Next steps and open questions:
- Build a small CLI that runs pre-cutover discovery and emits a deterministic Terraform input file for the new modules.
- Do we provide an optional managed NAT/proxy appliance for >100k monthly tokens to reduce egress scrutiny?
- Integrate BGP metrics into the Console routing dashboards for faster incident triage.

Appendix: quick Terraform snippet example (pseudo):
  module "tenant_vpc" {
    source = "git::https://gitlab.com/redwood/modules/vpc-core.git//v1"
    region = var.region
    cidr_block = var.tenant_cidr
    enable_flow_logs = true
  }

Feedback: add notes back to the linked JIRA or ping #private-deployments in Slack; file this under the private-deployments accelerators board when stable.
